blocks.text: That the bird דרור deror is not the swallow, as is held, but a kind of wild dove, namely the turtledove or the wood pigeon.

Among the birds there is one which the Hebrews call דרור deror, that is, freedom or free; מפני שדרה בבית כבשדה, because it dwells as freely in the house as in the field. So R. Ishmael determined in the Talmudic tractate Betsa, ch. 3, p. 24a. Hence the later Hebrews, and the recent lexicographers and interpreters of the Bible who have followed them, hold with the greatest unanimity that דרור deror is the swallow, because there are said to be two species of swallows,
of which one seeks the woods, the other enters under roofs. — — — — ^{a)}

But this reason is not sufficient, since there are also other birds that are partly domestic, partly wild. Among these the first place belongs to the doves, of which one kind is κατοικίδιον [katoikidion], domestic, the other νομαδικὸν [nomadikon], roaming, and feeding in the fields, as is found in Galen, book 10 On Simples. Varro also makes this distinction in On Agriculture, book 3, ch. 7, yet in such a way that he says both kinds dwell under roofs: but the wild kind in the highest part of towers, from which it flies out into the fields and returns, whereas the other, tamer kind, content with domestic food, usually feeds within the threshold of the door. For my part, I think that by the name דרור deror are meant both this wild kind of dove and whatever species of doves the Greeks list among the wild ones, but above all φάτταν [phattan], the wood pigeon, and τρυγόνα [trygona], the turtledove. I am moved to this, first, by the authority of the ancient interpreters, who explain דרור as either the turtledove or the wood pigeon. Thus in Ps. LXXXIV, 4 דרור is rendered turtledove in the Greek version, and in the Vulgate, the Chaldee, the Syriac, and both Arabic versions, and in the paraphrase of Apollinaris. But the Ethiopic has መዐንቅ፡, that is, the collared one: everyone knows that the wood pigeon is distinguished by this epithet, on account of the collar it has around its neck. Martial in the Xenia:
The collared wood pigeons slow and dull the loins.
